spec: Build a contact-form backend. Visitors submit messages with a name, email and message body; administrators can list all messages and delete individual ones. Messages are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single message store with create, list, and delete operations.

congruence_checklist: Message model has name, email, body

plan.summary: A JSON REST backend for a website contact form. Public visitors submit a message containing their name, email and message body; the service validates the input, timestamps it and persists it in a DynamoDB table. Administrators authenticate with a shared admin token and can list all stored messages (newest first, with pagination) and delete individual messages by id. The service is a standalone FastAPI application started by the harness that talks directly to DynamoDB via boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe reporting service status and DynamoDB table reachability.

Public endpoint for visitors to submit a contact message (name, email, message); validates fields, generates an id and created_at timestamp, writes the item to DynamoDB and returns the stored message with 201.
Admin-only listing of all contact messages via DynamoDB scan, sorted by created_at descending, with optional limit and next_token pagination.
Admin-only retrieval of a single contact message by id; 404 if not present.
Admin-only deletion of a single contact message by id; returns 204 on success, 404 if the message does not exist.

data_models.name: ContactMessage
fields: source_ip: str | None (request client IP, best effort)

aws_resources.name: contact-messages
aws_resources.justification: Primary datastore explicitly required by the spec; stores each submitted contact message with partition key `id` (string). PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; the app calls PutItem, GetItem, Scan and DeleteItem against it.

aws_resources.name: contact-form-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Execution identity assumed by the backend service, with an attached least-privilege policy granting only dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/Scan/DeleteItem/DescribeTable on the contact-messages table.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/contact-form-backend
aws_resources.justification: Log group the application writes structured request/error logs to, so administrators can audit submissions and deletions.

assumptions: Administrator authentication is not specified; the conventional minimal interpretation is used — admin endpoints (GET /messages, GET /messages/{id}, DELETE /messages/{id}) require an `X-Admin-Token` header compared against an ADMIN_TOKEN environment variable, returning 401 when missing/incorrect. No user accounts, Cognito or Secrets Manager resource is provisioned since the spec defines no credential store.
Message submission is fully synchronous: no email notification, SNS topic or SQS queue is required because the spec never mentions notifying anyone or asynchronous processing.
Message volume for a contact form is low, so a DynamoDB Scan with client-side sort by created_at is acceptable for listing; no secondary index is created.
Message ids are server-generated UUID4 strings; clients cannot supply their own id.
Timestamps are stored as ISO-8601 UTC strings in a `created_at` attribute.
Email is validated for format only; no verification email is sent.
Table names and the AWS endpoint URL (for LocalStack) are supplied to the app through environment variables (TABLE_NAME, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION).
There is no update/edit operation — the spec only lists create, list and delete.
Basic per-IP rate limiting and spam protection are out of scope as they are not mentioned; only payload size/length validation is enforced.
